newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies seen lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies seen lower.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while pork bellies were expected 0.250 to 0.750 cent lower, livestock analysts said.
Technical weakness and expectations for increased hog runs once farmers complete the bulk of spring planting could prompt weakness in hog futures, analysts said.

However, firmer cash hog prices early Wednesday on continued tight marketings and further strength in cash loin prices were cited as buying factors. Cash loins had been expected to top soon which weighed on futures Tuesday, they said.

There is growing speculation of export demand for loins. The time is drawing near that Japan would buy pork for import after July 1 when the "gate" price is lowered. Also, the yen has risen recently against the dollar, they added.

Pork belly futures were expected to open lower as demand for fresh bellies waned at the recent higher cash prices and increased supplies moved into storage. The weekly CME out-of-town storage report was considered bearish as it showed storings increasing, analysts said.
The market also looked technically weak after falling to a one-week low Tuesday, they said.
CME reported a net in-movement last week at out-of-town warehouses of 836,000 lbs versus an out-movement of 952,000 lbs last week and a net in-movement of 659,000 lbs last year.
